beats.say: This is a ten-frame. It is a box with ten places.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: A box with ten places, five on top and five below.

beats.say: Five places on top, five places below.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A counter is a dot that stands for one thing. Each place holds one counter.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: A dot that stands for one thing.

beats.say: Say one number for each counter, in order.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One, two, three, four, five.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The top row is full. The frame is not. Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The last number is ten, so this frame shows ten. A full frame is ten.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Here is another frame. It already has counters in it.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: It is a ten-frame, so it shows ten. Right?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: A ten-frame has ten places, but it shows only the counters in it.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Count them. One, two, three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The last number is three, so this frame shows three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Seven places are empty. An empty place is not a counter, so we do not count it.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Which frame shows nine counters? Here are four frames: A, B, C, D.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: B. I counted to nine in B, so B shows nine.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: When you fill a frame yourself, you stop at the number you want.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: B is already filled. Count every counter, to the last one.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Nine is not the last counter. One counter is still left. Ten.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: What number did the count end on?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Ten. So B shows ten, not nine.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Ten is one after nine, so B has one counter too many.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The last number you say tells how many. Count to the last counter.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Count every counter, to the last one. The last number said is how many.

beats.say: Now count the other frames the same way.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Frame A: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A ends on eight, one before nine, so it has one counter too few.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Frame C: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: C ends on nine. That is the number we were asked for.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Frame D has no counters, so there is nothing to count. That is zero.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Only C ends on nine. Frame C shows nine counters.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Which frame shows seventeen counters? Here are four frames: A, B, C, D.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Seventeen starts with seven. So I pick C. It has seven counters.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Count every counter in C, to the last counter.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The last number is seven. C shows seven counters, not seventeen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A frame holds only ten. How can seventeen fit?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: It does not fit in one frame. Seventeen needs a second frame.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Look at D. Its first frame is full. A full frame is ten.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Keep counting in the second frame. Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The last number is seventeen. D shows seventeen counters.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: How many counters are in the first frame? How many in the second?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Ten in the first frame. Seven in the second. Ten and seven more is seventeen.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: C has seven counters and no full ten. The full ten is part of seventeen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Now A. The first frame is full: ten. Then eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A ends on eighteen, one after seventeen. It has one counter too many.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Now B. Ten. Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: B ends on sixteen, one before seventeen. It has one counter too few.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Only D ends on seventeen. Frame D shows seventeen counters.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Every question like this goes the same way.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One. Count every counter, one number for each.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Count every counter, one number for each.

beats.say: Two. The last number I say is how many.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: The last number said is how many.

beats.say: Three. An empty place is not a counter.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: An empty place is not a counter.

beats.say: Four. A full frame is ten. Keep counting from there.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: A full frame is ten. Past ten, keep counting in the second frame.

beats.say: Five. Pick the frame whose last number is the number asked.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Choose the frame whose last number is the number asked.
